incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty incident triggered: network.lb.tls.handshake.failures — service: redwood-edge-lb, urgency: high. Pager assigned: Kai (oncall). Links: https://pagerduty.example/INC12345
Kai (oncall): acked. I'm looking now. TL;DR customers in EU seeing TLS handshake failures and 5xx on inference requests. Starting with ALB health and cert checks.
Priya (SRE): seeing spike in TLS handshake failures from 18:24 UTC -> spike in 525/524 on edge. CloudFront/ALB reports 'SSL handshake timeout' for ~18% of connections in eu-west-1.
Samir (NetEng): any recent cert rotations or edge config pushes?
Kai (oncall): not that I can see in deploy logs. Running quick curl against LB: `curl -v https://edge-eu.redwood.ai/health` -> TLS handshake resets intermittently.
Marta (Support): getting a handful of tickets saying "model responses failing mid-generation" and some 520 errors. Customer impact: a subset of EU customers intermittently failing, not all traffic. Escalation risk if sustained.
Priya (SRE): ALB target group in eu-west-1 shows ~25% targets unhealthy for short windows; target health logs show `TLS alert handshake_failure` to backend or client? Looks like LB failing on handshake with client side.
Samir (NetEng): checking DNS — nothing changed in hosted zone. TTLs normal (~60s). But I do see increased SYN retries to the ALB frontends in CloudWatch from certain edge nodes. Could be upstream network flapping causing TLS sessions to drop.
Kai (oncall): immediate mitigation plan: 1) fail traffic to secondary region (eu-central) for eu customers via weight shift; 2) rotate to fallback TLS profile on ALB (downgrade to allow broader ciphers temporarily); 3) enable aggressive connection retry/backoff at proxy layer. I'll coordinate 1 and 2 now.
Priya (SRE): +1 for regional weight shift. I'll prepare a canary shift 10% -> 50% if stable. Also pushing a temporary ALB config: `allowed_tls_versions: [TLSv1.2, TLSv1.3]` and expand ciphers to include ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 for compatibility.
Samir (NetEng): I'm ready to update Route53 weights. Before doing that, confirm certificate chain intact: `openssl s_client -connect edge-eu.redwood.ai:443 -servername edge-eu.redwood.ai` shows full chain and valid expiry (valid). Not a cert expiry.
Marta (Support): Notifying top-10 affected customers via status page and direct DM. Posting a short blurb: "We are investigating increased TLS handshake failures in EU; some requests may fail intermittently. Mitigations are in progress." :eyes:
incident-bot: PagerDuty note added: "Failover partial traffic to eu-central; ALB TLS profile relaxed; monitor 5xx/handshake metric."
Kai (oncall): Route53 weight change initiated: eu-west-1 -> 70%, eu-central -> 30% as a canary. Rolling now.
Priya (SRE): Metrics after 90s: EU 5xx rate down ~40% on eu-central targets, eu-west handshake failures reduced by ~30% after ALB TLS profile change. Connection timeouts still present but degraded.
Samir (NetEng): I'm seeing reduced SYN retry counts from some edge nodes. Might be transient peering / noisy neighbor. Will open ticket with cloud provider if it recurs.
Marta (Support): Updated status page and posted to customers list. Requesting ETA for full mitigation.
Kai (oncall): Next steps: 1) ramp eu-central to 50% if stable for 5m; 2) keep TLS profile relaxed for 30m while we collect telemetry; 3) contact cloud provider NOC with traceroutes from affected edge nodes.
Priya (SRE): Can we run quick curl load against canary: `ab -n 200 -c 10 https://edge-eu.redwood.ai/health` to confirm stability? I'm running it now from eu-central.
Kai (oncall): Running normal traffic routing change to 50/50. Do it carefully.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: INC12345 acknowledged by Kai.
Priya (SRE): Canary load shows stable 200/200 with small latencies. No handshake failures observed in canary region during test window.
Samir (NetEng): I've started collecting pcap from affected LB frontends and will upload to secure bucket: `s3://rdw-internal/pcap/inc12345/`. Opening cloud provider ticket #CP-98765 with these traces.
Marta (Support): Customer impact summary for incident record: "Intermittent TLS handshake failures causing 5xx responses for subset of EU customers between 18:24-19:02 UTC; partial traffic failover and ALB TLS profile relaxation reduced errors. No data loss; retries resulted in eventual success for many requests."
Kai (oncall): marking incident as mitigated for customer traffic at 19:03 UTC. Will keep on-call monitoring for 30m.
Priya (SRE): We'll keep TLS profile relaxed until root cause identified. Post-incident action items: 1) deep packet analysis with provider; 2) evaluate ALB edge node health checks and capacity; 3) consider increasing TLS handshake timeout/backoff on edge proxies; 4) playbook update for TLS handshake flaps.
Samir (NetEng): Provider responded to ticket acknowledging transient peering issue in eu-west-1 between two POPs — they claim mitigation deployed at 18:58 UTC. We should correlate.
Marta (Support): Creating follow-up status update for customers including timeline and recommended retry guidance.
Kai (oncall): Wrapping up. Incident -> mitigated. I'll create the incident postmortem draft and assign owners for the action items. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: Closing note logged to PagerDuty and creating internal incident doc at https://wiki.redwood/incident/INC12345
Priya (SRE): adding to backlog: run chaos tests to validate TLS handshake robustness across POPs.
Samir (NetEng): keeping watch; I put alarms to lower threshold for SYN retry spikes.
Marta (Support): Will follow up with impacted accounts tomorrow.
Kai (oncall): last check 19:15 UTC — metrics stable, no new pager events. Handing off to Priya for long-term follow-up.
Priya (SRE): acked and taking post-incident ownership.
Marta (Support): thanks team.
